newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 3.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 3. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto asked Indonesians to continue promoting national unity in order to achieve the goal of creating a prosperous nation based on the five principles in the national ideology of Pancasila.

More than 3,000 people in Sanggau Ledo district in Indonesia's Kalimantan province had fled to the city of Singkawang following a youth brawl which turned into tribal riots. At least five people were killed in the disturbances on Sunday.
President Suharto said that Indonesia and Thailand must foster cooperation, bilaterally and in the context of the Assocation of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
State-owned Bank Bumi Daya and privately-owned Bank Danamon pledged to loan a total of one trillion rupiah ($420 million) to the Federation of Village Cooperation.
Director of state-owned oil company Pertamina, Faisal Abda'oe, said Indonesia needed two more refineries by 2000 to meet burgeoning demand for fuel products.

The military said the three political parties: the ruling Golkar, Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and the Christian-nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are ready for the general elections in May.
